newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT -- Test higher seen in store for dlr/yen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -- Test higher seen in store for dlr/yen.

text.p: A determined dollar will likely clamber back above 110 yen and then push past 111 yen near-term in what some chartists deemed a continuation of a two-month uptrend.
"The overall August (and) September picture is an uptrend," said Ken Boyer, a technical analyst at MMS International. "So, we had a little bit of a correction last week but we recovered from that."
Thus Boyer said he is "bullish" towards short-term objectives of 110.58 yen, last week's high, and 111.16, the high from July 8.
A downside correction had pushed the U.S. currency lower to 108.80 yen last Wednesday, but the dollar managed to end the session above 109 yen.
On Monday, the U.S. unit stuck to narrow ranges, trading at 109.88/91 yen at 1517 EDT/1917 GMT, up marginally from 109.84/89 at the open.
Scott Siller, a senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch, also predicted dollar/yen appears to be on its way higher again but warned there is risk of a pullback to 109.50 yen.
Nevertheless, Siller contended the dollar could retest 110.62 yen and even higher to 111.20.
By contrast, the outlook for dollar/mark is not upbeat, according to chartists.
Siller pointed out that the dollar broke above a previous rally peak on Friday at 1.5175 marks but only managed to move up to 1.5190 marks.
"To me that looked like a false bull breakout," said Siller, adding that he expects the dollar to retest the areas of 1.5080 marks and 1.5050, key support levels in the two week range.
For his part, Boyer pegged 1.5067 marks as crucial support, calling this level the "trigger point" that would have to be broken to set a downside correction.
The dollar traded at 1.5122/27 marks at 1624 EDT/2024 GMT, down from 1.5155/60 marks at the opening.
Siller termed mark/yen as the catalyst for the expected rally in dollar/yen and the test lower in dollar/mark.

"We're thinking the 72.10 that was tested last week ... is going to hold and we're going to retest the upside again," Siller said. "We're back up to the 73.50 and 73.70 levels (in mark/yen)." -- Donna Sells 212-859-1668
